channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Taliban Official: Bagram Air Base Belongs to Afghanistan, Not the US
item.description: Anas Haqqani, a senior Taliban official, stated that Bagram Air Base rightfully belongs to Afghanistan and its people, not the United States. He criticized the base's history under foreign occupation, calling it a symbol of violence and imprisonment. Haqqani emphasized Afghan sovereignty and the right to self-determination.

item.title: Tajikistan and EU Discuss Parliamentary Cooperation in Brussels
item.description: Tajikistan and the European Union held their 13th Parliamentary Cooperation Committee meeting in Brussels on November 19. Discussions focused on enhancing inter-parliamentary ties, trade, economic relations, cultural and social connections, security threats, environmental policy, and cooperation in water, energy, transport, and infrastructure.

item.title: UN Warns of Growing Risk to Healthcare Access for Afghan Women and Girls
item.description: A UN official warned that 22 million women and girls in Afghanistan face an increasing risk of being deprived of healthcare. Taliban restrictions and reduced aid funding are hindering access, exacerbating the situation. The UN noted a rise in attacks on women's rights, impacting essential services.

item.title: Teenage Girl Sentenced to Eight Years for Murder in Turkestan Region
item.description: A teenage girl has been sentenced to eight years in prison for the murder of a 20-year-old man in Kazakhstan's Turkestan Region. The court found her guilty of premeditated murder, noting she had purchased a knife beforehand and later attempted to burn the victim's body. The defense's claim of attempted rape was not substantiated.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Doubling Compensation for Crime Victims
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs supports doubling the lump-sum compensation for crime victims. If approved, the maximum payment could increase from 216,250 to 432,500 tenge. The proposed increase aims to provide greater financial support to victims of various crimes, including human trafficking and severe bodily harm.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: MChS Official Detained in Connection with Child's Death
item.description: An former head of the MChS crisis management center, Azis Egemberdiev, has been detained in Kyrgyzstan as part of an investigation into the death of 14-year-old Amir Kunakov. He is suspected of abuse of office. The boy went missing in Ala-Archa park and was found two days later.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Kyrgyzaltyn Nearly Doubles Profit to 33.17 Billion Som in Nine Months
item.description: Kyrgyzaltyn reported a net profit of 33.17 billion som for January-September 2026, an 89.6% increase from the previous year. Investment income was the primary driver, reaching 31.64 billion som. Revenue from core operations also grew by 35.9% to 154.97 billion som.

item.title: Kazakhstan Can Earn from AI Training Data, Expert Says
item.description: Kazakhstan has the potential to gain a niche in the global market for collecting and labeling data for AI training, according to Konstantin Kolomeytsev of Sergek Group. The country's unique regional and linguistic specifics can provide valuable data unobtainable elsewhere. This data generation could become a major income source as automation impacts traditional jobs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Funds 90 Educational Facilities with Confiscated Corruption Proceeds
item.description: Kazakhstan has financed the construction of 90 educational facilities using funds confiscated from corrupt individuals, with 83 already operational. According to the Vice Minister of Education, approximately 159 billion tenge has been collected in a special fund since 2023, allocated for building and renovating educational institutions. This initiative aims to reduce school overcrowding and improve educational infrastructure.

item.title: Online Driving Theory Test Service Launched on Kazakhstan's eGov Platform
item.description: Kazakhstan has introduced an online service for booking driving theory tests via the eGov Mobile app. Applicants must have their driving school completion data confirmed in the system. The service checks for medical certificates and driving school completion before allowing candidates to select a license category and schedule their exam.

item.title: Russia Claims Downing 275 Ukrainian Drones Overnight
item.description: Russia's Defence Ministry announced it intercepted and destroyed 275 Ukrainian drones across various Russian regions, Crimea, and the Black Sea overnight. The ministry stated the interceptions occurred between Friday evening and Saturday morning Moscow time. This action is part of ongoing drone and missile attacks between Russia and Ukraine since February 2022.

item.title: Uzbekistan-Kazakhstan Border Crossing 'Chernyaevka' Set to Reopen November 25
item.description: The 'Gishtkuprik' border crossing, known as 'Chernyaevka,' between Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan is slated to resume operations on November 25, following extensive reconstruction. Sources in the Kazakh embassy indicated the reopening, which was delayed from its initial four-month renovation period. The upgraded crossing will significantly increase daily capacity.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Quarantine for Classes with 20% Student Absence Due to Illness
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement quarantine measures and transition classes to online learning if 20 percent of students are absent due to illness. This order, approved by the Ministry of Health, aims to curb the spread of flu and respiratory infections during the autumn-winter season. Regular health monitoring is in place in educational institutions.

item.title: Tajikistan and AIIB Discuss Investments in Environmental Infrastructure
item.description: Tajikistan and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) have discussed expanding cooperation and attracting investment for joint environmental protection projects. The meeting, held on the sidelines of COP31, focused on waste management systems, ecological parks, and ecotourism development. Both sides emphasized leveraging Tajikistan's natural potential for sustainable economic growth.

item.title: Cannabis Cultivation Laboratory Discovered and Dismantled in Kazakhstan's Mangystau Region
item.description: Authorities in Kazakhstan's Mangystau region have shut down an underground laboratory used for cultivating cannabis. During a search in October, 44 cannabis plants and related equipment, including lamps and timers, were seized. One individual suspected of organizing the lab's operation has been detained. An investigation into illegal cultivation for drug trafficking is underway.

item.title: Uzbekistan Digitalizes Water Payments and Expands Free E-Services
item.description: Uzbekistan has updated regulations for water payments and state services. Cash payments for water are now restricted to bank tellers, while more free electronic certificates are available to citizens. Changes aim to streamline service delivery and encourage digital transactions.

item.title: AI Agents to Reshape Labor Market Within a Year, Sergek Predicts
item.description: Sergek Group's AI director forecasts that companies will soon replace human specialists with autonomous AI agents, leading to significant workforce reductions. He predicts that individuals will need to master AI agents to remain competitive in the job market.

item.title: Russia Offers to Mediate Talks Between Afghanistan and Pakistan Amidst Tensions
item.description: Russia is prepared to facilitate negotiations between Afghanistan and Pakistan if requested by both nations, stated Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova. Moscow is monitoring the conflict and supports diplomatic solutions for regional peace and security. Zakharova emphasized collective counterterrorism efforts and socioeconomic development for Afghanistan.

item.title: New 550 MW Thermal Power Plant in Uzbekistan's Jizzakh Region Begins Generating Electricity
item.description: A new 550 MW thermal power plant in the Sharaf-Rashidov district of Uzbekistan's Jizzakh region has started supplying electricity to the national grid. The plant, a $500 million project with Turkish company Cengiz Enerji, is expected to produce up to 4.4 billion kWh annually and save 500 million cubic meters of natural gas.

item.title: Afghanistan Marks 80 Years of UN Membership, Reflecting on Diplomatic Journey and Challenges
item.description: Afghanistan joined the United Nations on November 19, 1946, marking 80 years of its diplomatic presence. UN membership provided a platform for Afghanistan to advocate for peace, development, and international law, while navigating foreign policy shifts and domestic developments. The UN Charter framework has guided its international relations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Implements New Rules for School Attendance Tracking and Bullying Prevention
item.description: Kazakhstan has enacted updated rules for tracking student attendance and preventing bullying, effective November 21. Local education authorities must maintain a database of children aged 0-18, flagging regular absences. Schools must now register bullying incidents within one business day and provide psychological support to victims.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Allowing Single Parents to Leave Work One Hour Early
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering amendments to its Labor Code that would allow single parents raising children under 14 to leave work one hour earlier. This benefit would apply to adoptive parents and guardians as well. The proposal aims to support parents, especially in large cities with traffic congestion.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Grants Tax Exemptions to Companies Supporting SCO Summit and Nomad Games
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has granted zero VAT rates on imports and a single tax exemption to two private companies and two state entities involved in supporting the SCO summit and the World Nomad Games. The tax relief, effective November 1, 2025, was approved on November 6, 2026, after the events concluded.

item.title: Kazakh National Security Committee Seeks Foreign National Williams Cole
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has issued a search notice for a 45-year-old foreign national named Williams Cole. The search was registered in the Turkistan region on November 21. The Saragash district police department is conducting the search, but details regarding Cole's nationality and the reasons for the search remain undisclosed.

item.title: S&P Raises Uzbekistan's Credit Rating to BB+, Highest in Country's History
item.description: S&P Global Ratings has upgraded Uzbekistan's credit rating to BB+, the highest level in the country's history. This upgrade brings Uzbekistan one step closer to achieving an investment-grade rating. The new rating reflects the country's improving economic stability and outlook.

item.title: Uzbekistan Police Seize Over 11.5 Kilograms of Hashish in Fergana Region
item.description: Law enforcement in Uzbekistan's Fergana region has disrupted a drug trafficking ring, seizing over 11.5 kilograms of hashish. A significant portion was found hidden among children's toys. One suspect was arrested selling 11 kilograms, with the drugs sourced from neighboring countries. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Strengthens International Cooperation in Judicial Expertise
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's judicial expertise service participated in an international conference on criminal procedure and judicial expertise in the digital age. The forum brought together experts from Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Moldova, and Azerbaijan to discuss the impact of digital technologies and artificial intelligence on legal proceedings.

item.title: UN University Rector Visits Almaty to Discuss Cooperation
item.description: Tshilidzi Marwala, Rector of the UN University and Under-Secretary-General, visited Almaty as part of his trip to Kazakhstan. He met with local officials and toured the "UN Plaza" hub, cultural, and educational sites. The visit focused on Almaty's potential and prospects for cooperation in education, science, and sustainable development between Kazakhstan and the UN.

item.title: Cities Without Greenery and Quiet: Urbanization's Toll on Tajikistan's Residents
item.description: Rapid urbanization in Tajikistan, especially the capital, leads to stress due to dense construction, traffic, and lack of trees. Residents report difficulties living in their cities, citing concerns about building quality and emergency access. Traffic congestion is a major issue, impacting daily life and services like taxis.

item.title: Tajikistan Discusses Aviation Development at ICAO Assembly in Canada
item.description: Tajikistan's Civil Aviation Agency Director participated in the 43rd ICAO Assembly in Montreal. Discussions focused on global civil aviation development, industry management, and international cooperation. Bilateral meetings were held to expand cooperation, increase flights, and open new routes.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Visa-Free Travel for 18 More Countries, Sugar Import Ban
item.description: Kyrgyzstan proposes visa-free entry for citizens of 18 additional countries, extending stay to 60 days. The Cabinet also banned white sugar imports for six months to address rising import levels. Changes to registration rules and pension benefits are also being discussed.

item.title: US Security Agencies Warn Airlines of Al-Qaeda Hijacking Threat
item.description: US security agencies, including the FBI and Department of Homeland Security, have alerted airlines and airports to recent messages from Al-Qaeda sympathizers encouraging hijackings similar to a past failed attempt. The warnings highlight calls to use aviation industry access for attacks.

item.title: Four Candidates Secure Over 30,000 Signatures for Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election
item.description: Four out of eleven individuals intending to run in Kyrgyzstan's 2027 presidential election have gathered the required 30,000 signatures. Current President Sadyr Japarov leads with over 60,000, followed by Aimen Kasenov, Ishak Masaliev, and Syimyk Japikeev. The signature collection period ends December 8.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Seeks Mutual Security Guarantees with Iran, Cites Regional Stability
item.description: Saudi Arabia's Special Representative for Negotiations, Manal Rezwan, called for mutual security guarantees with Iran, emphasizing that Saudi security is linked to regional stability. She noted that Iran-backed groups require tailored political approaches due to varying local conditions and influences.

item.title: Court Orders FlyArystan to Revise Passenger Transport Rules
item.description: A court has upheld a directive ordering FlyArystan to revise its internal passenger transport rules. The Ministry of Trade and Integration identified violations of consumer rights, including unilateral changes to transport conditions, limited carrier liability, and improper fee collection. The airline had challenged the directive.

item.title: BMW Driver Fined for Dangerous Drift on Dushanbe-Khujand-Chanak Highway
item.description: Traffic police in Tajikistan's Varzob district have fined a BMW driver for dangerous drifting on the Dushanbe-Khujand-Chanak highway. The driver, identified as Umedjon Marufjonovich Bachabekov from Dushanbe, was caught on video performing the maneuver on November 19, 2026. His actions were deemed a threat to himself and other road users.

item.title: Court Upholds Order for FlyArystan to Rectify Passenger Rights Violations
item.description: Courts have upheld a directive from Kazakhstan's Ministry of Trade and Integration ordering airline FlyArystan to correct violations of passenger rights. These included unilateral changes to terms, restricted liability, improper fees, and issues with refunds and consumer information. The airline's appeal was rejected.

item.title: Polio-Free Afghanistan Initiative Calls for Universal Vaccination of Children Under Five
item.description: The Polio-Free Afghanistan initiative is urging all children under five years old to be vaccinated against polio. The organization emphasizes that vaccination is crucial for protecting children's health and providing them with a healthy start in life. Afghanistan remains one of the countries still battling polio.

item.title: Taliban Restrictions Complicate Humanitarian Aid Delivery in Afghanistan, Expert Says
item.description: Afghanistan expert Susanne Schmeidl states that increasing Taliban restrictions make delivering humanitarian aid difficult without engaging with the group. Donor countries face a dilemma, and technical coordination is complicated by the need to separate aid from political engagement. The Taliban seeks greater control over aid operations.

item.title: Former Nvidia CEO Agrees to Testify Before US Senate Committee
item.description: Nvidia's former CEO, Jensen Huang, has agreed to testify before the US Senate Banking Committee. He is expected to answer questions regarding his relationship with entrepreneur Alice Huang, who is suspected of having ties to Chinese special services. The Senate will also discuss the illegal supply of American chips to China.
